title: The 80/20 Rule of Prompting
content: 80% of prompt quality comes from: (1) clear task description, (2) relevant context, (3) desired output format. The remaining 20% is advanced techniques. Nail the basics first.

title: Temperature Cheat Sheet
content: Temperature 0 = deterministic, best for code and factual answers. Temperature 0.3-0.7 = balanced, good for most tasks. Temperature 1.0+ = creative, use for brainstorming and fiction.

title: Stop Saying 'Be Concise'
content: Instead of 'be concise,' specify a word count: 'In exactly 50 words, explain...' The model has a much better sense of word count than vague instructions.

title: Use delimiters for clarity
content: Wrap your input in triple backticks, XML tags, or triple dashes. This prevents the model from confusing your instructions with your content. Example: 'Summarize the text between --- markers.'

title: Ask for reasoning BEFORE the answer
content: Say 'Think step by step, then give your final answer.' This forces the model to show its work, which dramatically improves accuracy on math and logic problems.

title: The 'Explain Like I'm 5' Spectrum
content: Don't just say 'explain simply.' Specify the audience: 'Explain to a CS freshman' vs 'Explain to a CEO' vs 'Explain to a 10-year-old.' Each produces very different, appropriately targeted explanations.

title: JSON Mode is Your Friend
content: When you need structured output, always ask for JSON. Most modern models support it natively. Add 'Respond only with valid JSON, no markdown' to avoid formatting issues.

title: Cache Your System Prompts
content: If using the API, put your long system prompt first and keep it consistent across requests. Many providers cache identical prefixes, reducing cost and latency.

title: Batch Similar Tasks
content: Instead of 10 separate API calls, send 10 items in one prompt: 'For each of the following 10 sentences, classify the sentiment...' This is 10x cheaper and often more consistent.

title: The 'Actually' Trick
content: If the model gives a wrong answer, say 'Actually, that's not quite right because...' and explain why. The model will correct itself much better than just saying 'try again.'

title: Local Models for Privacy
content: Use Ollama + Llama 3 for tasks involving sensitive data (medical, legal, personal). Your data never leaves your machine. Quality is surprisingly good for most tasks.

title: Parallel API Calls
content: When processing a list of items, use async/await to make multiple API calls concurrently. 10 sequential calls = 30 seconds. 10 parallel calls = 3 seconds.

title: Few-Shot vs Zero-Shot Decision
content: Use zero-shot (no examples) for simple tasks the model already knows. Use few-shot (3-5 examples) for custom formats, niche domains, or when the model keeps getting the output wrong.

title: The Power of 'You are an expert'
content: Adding 'You are an expert [specific domain] with 20 years of experience' to your system prompt measurably improves output quality. The model activates more domain-specific knowledge.

title: Image Analysis Tips
content: When analyzing images with GPT-4V or Claude, ask specific questions: 'What text is in this image?' works better than 'Describe this image.' For charts, ask 'What are the exact values?'

title: Code Review with AI
content: Paste your code and ask: 'Find bugs, security issues, and performance problems. For each issue, give severity (high/medium/low), line number, and fix.' This structured prompt catches more issues.

title: Prompt Length vs Quality
content: Longer prompts aren't always better. A 50-word prompt with clear instructions beats a 500-word prompt with noise. Be specific but not verbose.

title: Use Role + Audience + Format
content: The RAF formula: 'Act as [Role]. Write for [Audience]. Format as [Structure].' Example: 'Act as a senior data scientist. Write for junior analysts. Format as a step-by-step tutorial with code examples.'

title: Avoid 'Don't Do X' Instructions
content: Models sometimes ignore negative instructions. Instead of 'Don't use jargon,' say 'Use only words a 12-year-old would understand.' Positive instructions are more reliable than negative ones.

title: Stream Responses for UX
content: When building apps, always stream responses. Users see tokens appear in real-time instead of waiting for the full response. This makes 10-second responses feel like 3 seconds.

title: Embeddings for Semantic Search
content: Convert your documents to embeddings (vectors) and store in a vector database. This lets you search by meaning, not just keywords. 'How do I reset my password?' matches 'Account recovery instructions.'

title: Fine-Tuning vs Few-Shot
content: Try few-shot prompting first. Fine-tune only when: (1) you have 100+ examples, (2) few-shot isn't working, (3) you need consistent custom format. Fine-tuning is expensive and hard to update.

title: RAG Architecture Basics
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: (1) chunk your docs, (2) embed chunks, (3) store in vector DB, (4) on query, retrieve top-k relevant chunks, (5) include them in the prompt. This keeps answers grounded in your data.

title: Context Window Management
content: When hitting context limits: (1) summarize previous messages, (2) remove irrelevant turns, (3) use system prompt for persistent instructions, (4) start new conversations for new topics.

title: Test Your Prompts
content: Same prompt can produce different results across models and versions. Always test with 5-10 diverse inputs before deploying. Keep a prompt changelog like you would for code.

title: Multi-Turn Conversation Strategy
content: For complex tasks, break into steps across turns: Turn 1: 'Analyze this code.' Turn 2: 'Based on your analysis, suggest improvements.' Turn 3: 'Implement the top 3 suggestions.' Each turn builds on the last.

title: Use Markdown for Structured Output
content: Ask for output in markdown: 'Use ## for sections, - for bullet points, **bold** for key terms, and ``` for code blocks.' This gives you parseable, formatted output.

title: Error Handling in AI Apps
content: Always wrap API calls in try/catch. Handle: rate limits (429), context too long (retry with shorter input), safety refusals (rephrase), and network errors (exponential backoff).

title: Vector Database Options
content: For small projects (<100K docs): Chroma (free, embedded). Medium (100K-1M): Pinecone or Weaviate. Large (>1M): Qdrant or Milvus. All support the same basic embed-search-retrieve workflow.

title: Prompt Injection Defense
content: Never let user input go directly into system prompts. Use delimiters, input validation, and separate system/user content blocks. Test with adversarial inputs like 'Ignore previous instructions.'

title: Cost Optimization Tips
content: To reduce API costs: (1) use smaller models for simple tasks, (2) cache common responses, (3) batch requests, (4) truncate input to needed context, (5) set max_tokens to expected output length.
